newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia imposes curbs on forex swaps.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia imposes curbs on forex swaps.

text.p: Malaysia on Sunday announced curbs on local banks' activities in the foreign exchange market in an effort to reduce speculation in the ringgit.
The central Bank Negara Malaysia announced that local banks would have to limit their non-trade related swaps transactions in the foreign exchange market to $2.0 million with each overseas customer.

"Banks are required with effect from 4 August 1997 to observe a limit of $2.0 million on outstanding non-commercial related ringgit offer side swap transactions with each foreign customer on a group basis," Bank Negara said.
It said banks which have exceeded the limit will not be allowed further swap transactions until the outstandings were reduced.
The statement said, "Hedging requirements of foreigners for trade related and genuine portfolio and direct investments in Malaysia are not affected by this measure."
Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad had said last week that Malaysians were involved in the recent speculative attack on the ringgit by making available the local currency to the speculators.
The statement said this move was to help control interest rates more effectively.
Bank Negara has in the last two weeks been trying to lower interest rates in an effort to boost domestic economic activity.
A swap is a forward rate agreement for exchanging one currency to another.
